# dlarrr

> Tests whether a symmetric tridiagonal matrix warrants expensive computations for high relative accuracy.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlarrr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlarrr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlarrr( N, d, strideD, e, strideE ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Output array |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix. $N > 0$.
- `d`: The N diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `e`: On entry, the first (N-1) entries contain the subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T; `E(N)` is set to ZERO.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlarrr.ndarray( N, d, strideD, offsetD, e, strideE, offsetE ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Output array |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| ↳ `offsetE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `e` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix. $N > 0$.
- `d`: The N diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `e`: On entry, the first (N-1) entries contain the subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T; `E(N)` is set to ZERO.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N <= 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

`INFO` = 0(default) : the matrix warrants computations preserving

relative accuracy.

`INFO = 1` : the matrix warrants computations guaranteeing

only absolute accuracy.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlarrr()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLARRR`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlarrr.f).
-   The function returns `0` if the matrix may be relatively robust, indicating that expensive computations guaranteeing high relative accuracy in eigenvalues are warranted. It returns `1` if standard methods should be used instead.
-   The routine checks whether `sqrt(|d(i)|)` is sufficiently large and whether the accumulated off-diagonal ratios remain below a threshold (`RELCOND = 0.999`).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlarrr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlarrr';

// Well-conditioned tridiagonal matrix:
let d = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0 ] );
let e = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 ] );

let info = dlarrr( 5, d, 1, e, 1 );
console.log( 'Well-conditioned INFO:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 0

// Poorly-conditioned tridiagonal matrix:
d = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 ] );
e = new Float64Array( [ 0.99, 0.99, 0.99 ] );

info = dlarrr( 4, d, 1, e, 1 );
console.log( 'Poorly-conditioned INFO:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 1
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
